question: Which state belongs to one document, shared root or mounted view, and can competing lifetime owners be removed?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest stop verdict, at queue position 4 in the plite-core group. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: One document owns roots, meta, plugin registry and commits; shared roots are never copied per view.
Each view keeps its own root binding, focus, composition, read-only state, authored projection and plugin API identity.
A view of a view reads the runtime owner and keeps the source's document, read-only state and authored mode; derivation never unlocks read-only (docs/vision/plite.md).
The primary root is implicit; explicit roots address additional roots only.
Independent editors share no document state, even under one toolbar.
View-local resources retire with their mounted view.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-11 lifetime comparison and the 2026-09-30 content-root design, execution and closure records. Rechecked on the live tree the runtime, owner and root weak maps in editor-runtime.ts, view derivation in createEditorViewRuntime, the new private editor-view-lifetime.ts, EditorRoot's owner check, the production createEditorView callers via git grep, and the absence of public useRuntime and RuntimeValue. The ledger marks the content-root executions' proof stale, and it was not rerun.
summary: The job is to separate what one document owns (roots, meta, registry, commits) from what each view owns (root binding, focus, composition, read-only state, authored projection, mounted resources). Live source keeps one runtime per document in private weak maps. createEditorView binds every view, including a view of a view, to that owner and keeps the source view's document, sticky read-only state and authored mode, as the 2026-09-30 content-root execution adopted. A private view-lifetime registry retires view-local resources such as Yjs awareness. Production uses every view kind, including AI chat root and accepted and proposed authored views, static, plain-text and HTML document views, and EditorRoot with a named root. The public React Runtime, useRuntime and RuntimeValue are gone, and type tests assert it. The strongest cuts lose. Explicit roots on every call bring view state back as caller adapters, a static editor per document recompiles the plugin graph per render, and one document per view or one global store breaks synced blocks or independent editors. Keep the current design.

alternatives: Keeping the current design wins. A private document owner with root-, document- and authored-bound views covers every observed consumer without another public object.

Deleting views and passing an explicit root and policy on every call loses. Base path inputs address the main root by law, so root-relative paths, per-view focus, composition and read-only state, and AIChatPlugin's accepted and proposed projections would reappear as caller adapters.

Replacing document-bound views with a fresh static editor per rendered document loses. Static rendering, plain-text and HTML serialization would recompile the plugin graph per document, while the document view borrows the compiled schema, is forced read-only and now caches only owned documents.
One independent document per view loses, because it duplicates shared roots and their commits (synced-blocks, multi-root-document).
One global editor store loses, because it conflates independent editors (multiple-editors-demo) that share only toolbar targeting.
Re-exposing the runtime as a public React object loses. The Runtime, useRuntime and RuntimeValue cut landed, and generic-react-editor-contract.tsx asserts the removal.

Taking MAIN_ROOT_KEY off the plitejs root fixes a real leak against the implicit-primary-root law, but distribution's 2026-10-04 Pursue owns the @internal root values, and it does not change lifetime ownership.
proofLimits: Source read only; no headless view contracts, browser multi-editor proof, mounted focus or composition, or cache-scale run was repeated, and the content-root executions' receipts are marked stale by the ledger. editor-runtime-view.ts has uncommitted model-admission hunks (view document cache, root snapshot reader), but the view-derivation code this verdict rests on is committed apart from formatting.
